text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.

GERMANY - Bunds pare some gains after slew of stronger than expected U.S. data indicating consumer spending may rise, leading to fears of higher inflation. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.40, up 0.03 from Tuesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK gilts settle lower as markets digest Tuesday's budget, see continued pressure for further rate rises. Bund spreads widen, curve steepens, short sterling gives up Tuesday's four bps gain. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 110-19/32, down 14/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - PIBOR settled up with firmer franc, bond futures give up gains after Chicago purchasing managers, hit new high of 128.28 earlier. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.08, down 0.02 from Tuesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt markets softer at finish but more through lack of direction than activity to push them down, dealers say. Traders say reasonable volume due to spread activity between December and March LIFFE contracts. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 127.94, down 0.06 from Tuesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - US Treasuries trim some gains, but still firm near midday, with profit-take sets in after some stronger-than-expected data, underlying sentiment still seen bullish, flows slow as market heads to an early close, retailers hold positions, foreigners still buying dips. The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 115-07/32, down 04/32 from Tuesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.44 percent.

JAPAN - Cash Japanese government bonds (JGBs) and futures rocketed on a variety of bullish factors, such as only a slight recovery in business sentiment as seen in the Bank of Japan's key quarterly "tankan" corporate survey and falls in key money market rates, traders said. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 126.04, up 0.49 from Tuesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Primary market activity slowed appreciably with just a handful of retail deals emerging ahead of Thursday's U.S. holiday. The major develpment came overnight when an Ecuadorean finance ministry offical said the country's proposed Eurobond would be a $400 Eurobond five-year deal priced 350 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
